NEGROES WANTED BY MOB RUSHED TO MACON JAIL
a prominent Twiggs county farmer, was brought to the Bibb county jail this morning by Sheriff Wimberly to escape a mob that was forming to take him from the jail and lynch the negro. ernest-chappell-fitzpatrick-1915-08-02.A2:
NEGROES IN DANGER.
Threatened Lynching Directed at Alleged Assailant and One Who Stole Cow.
Macon, Ga., Aug 1.—Two negroes were rushed to this city at midnight from Fitzpatrick in Twiggs county to prevent a threatened lynching there. One of the negroes, Ernest Chappell, is said to have confessed that he attempted to assault a white woman; the other, Will Thomas, is accused of stealing a cow. Both were in jail at Fitzpatrick when the sheriff learned that a mob was organizing to lynch the one accused of attempted assault and he then brought them here for safekeeping.

walter-tucker-brownsville-1915-08.A1:
Officer Kills Negro.
waville — Walter Tucker
Officer Kills Negro.
Brownsville.—Walter Tucker, aged 27, while resisting arrest on Aug. 23 was shot to death by Marshal James Walker of this city. Tucker refused to be arrested, and started toward the officer when the fatal shot was fired. The negro recently returned from the penitentiary.
